kicker: Where to use a decision model

scenes.headline: Where a decision model belongs in your system
scenes.sub: Jev picks from a list you send. Four questions decide where that works.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Kumquat! A decision model like Jev never writes: it picks from a list you send. Here's where it fits.

scenes.text: A decision model picks from a list you send. Each option is scored alone, and they meet only in a softmax, so no option can read another.
scenes.say: The key fact: each option is scored alone, and options meet only in a final softmax. So no option can read another.

steps.say: Your code builds the option list. The model can only answer from it.
Each option is encoded in its own row, beside the state and question, and comes out as one number.
The options first meet in a softmax, after every forward pass has finished.
Then code does the rest: take the top option, or branch on its probability.

scenes.title: As the vendor drew it
scenes.credit: docs.typesafe.ai, the pre-parsed value extraction cookbook

steps.say: The vendor drew the same procedure: regex finds candidate values, and downstream code acts on the one picked.
The highlighted box is the only part the model does: pick the one that fits.

items.say: One: is the answer set finite, and known before the call?
Two: can code you own enumerate it? That's where the work is.

items.text: Can each option be judged alone?
items.say: Three: can each option be judged without reading another? If not, relate them in code, and ask about one pair.

items.text: Is the list frozen before you branch?
items.say: Four: is the list frozen before you branch? Add paraphrases of the right answer, and its probability falls from point six one nine to point two one five.

scenes.title: Relational choice: 100 cases, accuracy
scenes.note: shared context is necessary, and nowhere near sufficient
scenes.say: Where one option refers to another, Jev scores zero of a hundred. Letting options see each other isn't enough: a bidirectional encoder scores eight.

scenes.text: The test is whether one option can read another. It's the one gate money cannot buy back.
scenes.say: The test is whether one option can read another. Cost and latency aren't gates; money can't buy this one back.

recap: Code builds the list; the model picks from it
Options are scored alone and meet in a softmax
Relations between options belong in code
scenes.say: To recap: code builds the list, each option is scored alone, and relations belong in code.
